html:
The fall of Tenochtitlan was the capture of the Aztec capital by Spanish conquistadors and their Indigenous allies, after a siege of about three months that ended on 13 August 1521.

Hernán Cortés had first entered the island city in 1519 as a guest of Moctezuma II, then took him hostage. In 1520 the city rose against the Spanish. Moctezuma was killed, and the Spanish fled at night with heavy losses. Cortés regrouped in Tlaxcala, the Aztecs' old enemy.

The return was not a Spanish invasion so much as a war of many Indigenous cities against Tenochtitlan. Tens of thousands of Tlaxcalan and other warriors fought with a few hundred Spaniards. Cortés's interpreter and adviser, the Nahua woman known as Malinche, helped him bargain with them. The Spanish built small boats to control the lake, cut the causeways and the aqueduct, and fought their way in street by street.

Disease did much of the work. Smallpox had swept through the city in 1520, killing the new emperor Cuitláhuac and many others. The last emperor, Cuauhtémoc, was captured as he tried to escape by canoe.

The city was left in ruins, and the Spanish built Mexico City on top of it. The fall opened the way for Spanish rule over Mexico and much of the Americas, though conquest of other peoples, like the Maya, took far longer.
sum: The fall of Tenochtitlan was the capture of the Aztec capital by Spanish conquistadors and their Indigenous allies, after a siege of about three months that ended on 13 August 1521.
